claim: Urban et al. report a 25.2% reduction in heat-attributable mortality associated with HPP implementation across 102 locations.
support: paper reports 25.2% (95% CI 19.8%-31.9%), about 1.8/100,000 and 14,551 deaths under its model
upper_bound: reported cross-location observational model estimate; not a universal fixed causal effect
missing_or_competing: U1 uses national HPP metadata and no public raw mortality; G1 has no pooled protective effect before city-variable adjustment

claim: The Urban three-stage analysis can be fully reproduced from the public package.
support: later-stage coefficients, metadata and outputs are public
upper_bound: bounded static and output audit only
missing_or_competing: raw MCC mortality input and R environment/dependencies are unavailable; stage 1 cannot be rerun from the zip alone

claim: The public implementation has a simulation/reporting discrepancy requiring adjudication.
support: stage 3 sets 1000 simulations and raw outputs have 1000 simulation columns; stage 4 repeatedly selects 1:100
upper_bound: a code-level interval audit issue, not yet proof that the headline estimate changes
missing_or_competing: exact paper-to-script path and effect on every reported CI must be checked in analysis/challenge

claim: The treatment variable is not equivalent to actual local implementation.
support: U1 uses national HPP catalogues/metadata; WHO separates implementation monitoring from evaluation; G1 cannot disentangle warning from dissemination/actions
upper_bound: plan/HWS metadata can be treated as a proxy exposure in the studied design
missing_or_competing: local activation, delivery, coverage and cross-agency resources are not observed here

claim: The association is robust to major alternative specifications and extreme-year removal.
support: U1 reports 15.2% after excluding summer 2003 and reports no significant regional/class heterogeneity
upper_bound: directional association under the reported specifications
missing_or_competing: U1 limitations include trends and metadata uncertainty; G1 has non-ideal visual pre-trends in 8/15 cities and heterogeneity

claim: Independent quasi-experimental evidence shows an overall protective effect of heat warning/action systems.
support: G1 pooled RR 1.00 (0.98-1.01), with RR 0.85 (0.75-0.97) after city-variable adjustment; M1 finds mixed/no reductions in most evaluations
upper_bound: city- and specification-dependent evidence; not a universal null or universal benefit
missing_or_competing: G1 warning classification and implementation cannot be separated; review evidence is heterogeneous

claim: The 102-location result identifies which HPP element caused the mortality reduction.
support: U1 estimates a composite HPP proxy; its limitations say metadata may not reflect local reality
missing_or_competing: actual intervention receipt, intensity, timing and coverage not available
